title: runtime: the package doors record whatever `actor` the request body names — publish, save, discard, revert, rollback, reassign and duplicate write a caller-chosen name into metadata history
body:
epic:#28130#1 · hotlong · session_040dfd80c4c9411b895c698e785a6848

Filing gate: ① defect, read in code at `origin/main` `63a9bcb773` (not executed end to end) · reach: any caller holding `manage_metadata` on the package REST doors · found while drafting N-06 (#28406) and split out on the reviewer's recommendation; maintainer, verbatim, in the desktop PM session: 「同意」. ⛔ Not a claim.

Part of #28236 (split from N-06) · lane: `domain:server` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`) · size: S–M.

**Business reason.** Metadata history and package commits are the record an administrator reads to decide what to roll back and whom to ask. Today the package doors write into that record whatever name the request body supplies, so a caller who may edit metadata can make a change look as if someone else made it. The single-item door already records the authenticated user; the package doors should follow the same rule.

**Measured (`63a9bcb773`).** Seven doors in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` pass `...(body?.actor ? { actor: body.actor } : {})` straight into the protocol:
- `:1891` → `protocol.publishPackageDrafts` (publish-drafts — N-06 fixes this one)
- `:2074` → `protocol.saveMetaItem`
- `:2239` → `protocol.discardPackageDrafts`
- `:2301` → `protocol.revertCommit`
- `:2327` → `protocol.rollbackToPackageCommit`
- `:2422` → `protocol.reassignOrphanedMetadata`
- `:2467` → `protocol.duplicatePackage`

Nothing between the route and the protocol replaces it; the protocol stamps `request.actor` into history rows and package commits. The contrast: `packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts:619` takes `const actor = await this.resolveMetaWriteActor(environmentId, req)` and its comment says `X-Actor` is not consulted. Not verified: what the console sends today on each door (publish-drafts sends an empty body per N-06's reading, so its rows fall back to the protocol default).

**Wanted.**
1. Every door above records the request's authenticated identity through the same resolver the single-item door uses (`resolveMetaWriteActor`, or its runtime-side equivalent); a body `actor` is ignored on all seven. One helper, not seven copies.
2. If a door has a real caller that must act on behalf of another identity (a system job, a CLI ceremony), that caller is named in the PR and served by an explicit server-side path, never by trusting the body.
3. The request schemas in `packages/spec` that declare `actor` as a client field drop it or mark it ignored (Zod first; route ledger, SDK client and OpenAPI regenerated); `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` lines filled truthfully.
4. Coordinate with N-06 (#28406): whichever lands first owns the shared helper; the other consumes it. N-06 keeps the change-note work.

**Tests.** For each of the seven doors: a body naming another user records the session user, with an ablation (restore the pass-through → the test goes red). An unauthenticated or system call keeps today's documented fallback.

**Not here.** The change note and the display name in Studio's history panel (N-06). Audit-log (`sys_audit`) actor capture — a different writer.

**Dedupe.** #22510 (closed; `sys_activity.actor_name`, record history, not metadata history). Searched `body.actor`, `actor spoof`, `publish-drafts actor`, `history actor`: no open card.

Links back: #28236, #28406, ADR-0146 D1, ADR-0067.
